sections.h2: Quickest way to sell in Lower Macungie Township
sections.html:
Owners here choose between an agent listing, a private sale and a cash offer, and the cash route usually closes soonest because no buyer's lender is waiting on an appraisal. Whichever route you pick, the township's building sewer inspection and the deed recording at the county Recorder of Deeds still have to happen before the keys change hands.

Lower Macungie sits in southern Lehigh County, about 7 miles southwest of Allentown. It has about 33,507 people, and the township grew from 16,871 residents in 1990 to 30,633 in 2010, so much of the housing is fairly recent. Nearly all of it is owner occupied, which means most sales are a family selling the home they live in. Turnover is low, so a house that needs repairs or comes with tenants stands out. Sellers who ask for a fast close are often handling an inherited house, a job move, a divorce, a rental with tenants, or a roof and mechanical systems that need money they would rather not spend.

  • A cash buyer purchases the house in its current condition, so you skip showings and listing prep.
  • You pick the closing date, which helps when a move or an estate settlement has a hard deadline.
  • The sewer inspection result, the sewer and trash certification and the transfer tax still belong in the plan, so ask who handles each one before you sign.

Buyers in the area often start with the East Penn School District name, so it belongs in any listing conversation. Winters are cold, with January averages near 29 degrees, so expect a buyer's inspector to look hard at the roof, gutters and basement.

Before any sale or transfer, the township wants a building sewer inspection on file. The inspection looks at the private sewer line that runs from the house to the township's sewer lateral, a pipe the owner, not the township, is responsible for.

  • A Journeyman or Master Plumber must perform the video inspection and submit a complete Building Sewer Inspection Report, a copy of the video and proof of licensure to the township.
  • Emailed or uploaded video files are rejected. Hand in a physical copy, ideally a USB flash drive, which stays in the property file for at least five years.
  • Public works staff review what you send, then mail the owner a pass or fail letter, with an email copy if the report gave an address.
  • A failed line means the owner fixes it before the sale. A passing result is valid for up to two years.

The township posts a list of plumbers whose credentials are on file. Any other plumber works too, as long as proof of licensure goes in with the report. The point of the program is to keep stormwater and groundwater out of private lines, since that extra flow adds to overflows at the Allentown wastewater plant. The ordinance also covers transfer without inspection, so call the township office at 610-966-4343 before you assume anything about timing.

sections.h2: Bills and taxes at a Lower Macungie closing
sections.html:
Four items show up on a Lower Macungie settlement: a sewer and trash certification, the sewer inspection record, and state and local transfer tax. Each runs through a different office with a different wait, so open them the day the agreement is signed.

  • Sewer and trash certification: the township's utility billing office issues it for a sale or refinance for a $50 fee, and the check has to arrive before processing starts. Sewer and trash bills go out quarterly and are due within 30 days.
  • Past due utility balances: once an amount is more than 90 days late it goes to a collection law firm and drops off township invoices, so clear it before closing.
  • Pennsylvania realty transfer tax: 1 percent of the value, collected by the county Recorder of Deeds, and both buyer and seller are jointly liable.
  • Local transfer tax: the township ordinance sets its share at one half of one percent, and the township and any other taxing body together may not exceed 1 percent. Ask your title company for the school district's share and who pays what under your contract.

Lehigh County Authority bills water on its own, which means the final water reading is a separate phone call. Some transfers owe no state transfer tax, such as certain family transfers and property passed by will or intestacy, so ask the title company whether an inherited house qualifies.

Your assessed value comes from the 2013 base year, when Lehigh County last reassessed every parcel at 100 percent of fair market value. Only new construction or demolition changes it since. To appeal, get an original signed form plus the filing fee to the Board of Assessment Appeals by August 1. A postmark or a fax will not save a late filing. If you received a Change of Assessment Notice, the date printed on it is your deadline.

If you are selling a rental or other property you do not live in, a 2026 Pennsylvania law requires non-owner-occupant owners to file contact information with the county within 30 days of buying. Owner-occupied principal residences are exempt, so the rule matters mostly to the investor who buys from you.

sections.h2: What if the house needs repairs or has tenants?
sections.html:
You can still sell it, and the sewer line is the first item to sort out. Order the video inspection early, because a failed line means repair work before closing and the township mails the pass or fail letter, which takes time. If a buyer will take the house as-is, ask whether that includes sewer repairs and who pays, and put the answer in the contract.

For tenants, review the lease end date and security deposit handling with your attorney, and ask the township office about any rental rules that apply to the address. Keep copies of the sewer inspection letter, the utility certification and the deed, since the buyer's title company will ask for them.

A workable order is to book the plumber first, then request the $50 sewer and trash certification, then ask the title company to total the transfer tax. A cash buyer will not wait on a lender, but the pass or fail letter and the certification still set the earliest closing date.

faqs.q: Do I need an inspection to sell a house in Lower Macungie Township?
faqs.a: Yes, a building sewer video inspection by a Journeyman or Master Plumber is required before a sale or transfer. The township reviews it and mails a pass or fail letter, and a passing result stays valid for up to two years.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax when selling in Lower Macungie?
faqs.a: The contract decides, but the law makes buyer and seller jointly liable. The state rate is 1 percent and the township's local rate is one half of one percent, with the county Recorder of Deeds collecting at recording.

faqs.q: How much is the sewer and trash certification in Lower Macungie?
faqs.a: The township charges $50 for a sewer and trash certification used for a sale or refinance. Email the utility billing office and mail the check, which must arrive before processing begins.

faqs.q: When is the deadline to appeal an assessment in Lehigh County?
faqs.a: Annual appeals are due on or before August 1 of each year. The original signed form and filing fee must be received by then, because postmarks and faxes are not accepted.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Lower Macungie Township?
faqs.a: East Penn School District serves it. High school students go to Emmaus High School, and the township has Eyer Middle School, Lower Macungie Middle School, Wescosville Elementary and Willow Lane Elementary nearby.
